plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-composer-launcher

**One "+" panel for compositions, plugins and MCP.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

> 🟢 **Collision risk: very low.** This is a **pure UI plugin with no server-side seam at all** — it never rewrites requests, tool results or the system prompt, so the "functional collision" layer does not apply. All **four** client slots it takes are `list` / `keyed`, never `chain`. See [Compatibility](#compatibility).

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-4c6ef5.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Host](https://img.shields.io/badge/host-desktop%20%7C%20web-2f9e44.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility)

**The composer's `+` button, turned into a real menu.**

---

## Table of contents

- [What this is](#what-this-is)
- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)
- [Settings](#settings)
- [HTTP routes](#http-routes)
- [Interface language](#interface-language)
- [🔗 Integration](#-integration)
- [Known limitations (stated plainly)](#known-limitations-stated-plainly)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
- [Self-check](#self-check)
- [License](#license)

---

## What this is

By default the `+` button left of the composer opens a file picker. Everything else you may want to point the model at — a browser tab you are looking at, an earlier conversation, a skill, an MCP server, one of the plugins installed on this machine — has to be typed by hand, or referenced with `@`.

`dsh-composer-launcher` replaces that button with a **three-group menu**:

| Group | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Add** | files and folders, earlier chats, plan mode, goal mode |
| **Capabilities** | slash commands, skills, MCP servers |
| **Common plugins** | one row per installed plugin, plus an "all plugins" row |

What you pick does not get pasted in as text. It becomes a **reference chip** on a rail above the input box — the same native chip kind the host already renders for `@` references — and only turns into message text when you actually send.

There is also an **optional browser extension** (`DSH Tab Bridge`) which pushes your real browser's tabs to the plugin over a loopback HTTP bridge, so the Tabs row lists the pages you genuinely have open rather than a throwaway debug instance.

---

## What it does

### 1. The `+` menu (three groups)

A 360px panel, opened from the button at the `conversation.input.left` slot.

- **Add** — *Files and folders* (the host's own picker, multi-select, drag-and-drop; falls back to `@` references when the host exposes no folder picker), *Chats* (via `remote.sessionReferenceResolver`; chats only, no files), *Plan*, *Goal*.
- **Capabilities** — *Commands* (whatever the host's slash-command service offers), *Skills* (read live with `ctx.remote.skills.list({ sessionId })`), *MCP* (needs the host's `remote.mcpManager`).
- **Common plugins** — one row per plugin returned by `ctx.remote.pluginInventory.list()`. That list is read from the host on every load, so installing, removing or disabling a plugin is reflected immediately and there is no cache to keep in sync. Three modes decide which rows appear: `pinned`, `frequent`, `mixed` (see [Settings](#settings)).

Every row can be switched off individually from the settings card.

### 2. Reference chips

Picked items land on a rail **above** the input box (`conversation.input.dock`). A chip is `{ label, kind, icon }` plus an optional `url`, where `kind` is one of `web`, `plugin`, `skill`, `mcp`. Clicking the `×` removes it.

Two properties are worth naming, because both were bugs before they were features:

- **A web chip keeps its address.** A page title with no URL is useless to whoever reads the message — the chip carries the URL and the payload includes it.
- **A session reference stays a chip.** Writing a reference back through the plain-text draft API silently downgrades it to body text; the plugin renders it as a chip instead and never round-trips it through the text editor.

Chips are **per session**, so two chat tabs never share a rail.

On send, each chip is serialised into the message with a short marker, so the model can tell a referenced page from an attached file:

| Chip kind | Marker |
|---|---|
| web page | `【参考网页】<title> — <url>` |
| plugin | `【使用插件】<name>` |
| skill | `【技能】<name>` |
| MCP server | `【MCP】<name>` |

> These markers are literal and stay in Chinese in both interface languages. They are part of the text the **model** reads, not interface copy — translating them would change what the model sees.

### 3. Settings card

Registered on the `settings.plugin.item` slot as a card titled **Launcher** — 「启动器」 in the Chinese interface. It is collapsed the first time you open it and remembers that choice. All twelve fields are listed under [Settings](#settings).

### 4. Debug browser (fallback)

The Tabs row can also read tabs over a remote-debugging port from a Chromium process it starts itself. That is what **Launch debug browser** does — and when the extension is staged, the same call attaches it with `--load-extension` and then verifies through the debugging port that it really mounted, so this route needs no manual step at all (see [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)). It stays a fallback rather than the primary path because it only ever sees that one throwaway-profile instance, never the browser you already have open.

### 5. Loopback bridge

The host half owns a small HTTP bridge on `127.0.0.1:43130` (override: `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT`) so the extension can push tabs into it. It binds loopback only, yields politely if an older instance already holds the port, and is used for nothing else.

---

## Screenshots

**The `+` menu — Add / Capabilities / Common plugins — with the Tabs row fed by the extension**

![The composer + menu with the Tabs group and the connected extension](screenshots/01-composer-menu-tab-bridge.png)

**The Tabs row reading a real Microsoft Edge window over the bridge**

![Tab list pushed from Microsoft Edge](screenshots/02-tab-list-edge.png)

**The MCP servers the Capabilities group can reference — the row is built from the host's `remote.mcpManager`**

![MCP servers listed by the host](screenshots/03-mcp-servers.png)

**The plugin inventory the Common plugins group is built from, including its "N / M" narrowing counter**

![Plugin inventory with composition filtering](screenshots/04-plugin-inventory.png)

---

## The browser extension

The plugin works without it — the Tabs row simply says the extension is not installed and points at the button. With it, the row lists the tabs of your **everyday browser**.

### Three ways to get it loaded

Chromium will not let anything silently sideload an extension into the browser you use every day. That is a browser security rule with no plugin-side workaround, so the goal is a different one: make every *remaining* step either automatic or one click.

| Route | What happens | Manual steps |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a browser this plugin starts** | The plugin spawns a separate Chromium process with `--load-extension` pointing at the staged copy, then **verifies through the debugging port that the extension really mounted** | none |
| **B — your everyday browser** | The Tabs row offers *Open the extensions page* and *Copy the extension path*, so loading it once is a paste and a "Load unpacked" | one time, ~20 seconds |
| **C — managed machines** | Chromium enterprise policy (`ExtensionSettings` / `ExtensionInstallForcelist`) pointing at a self-hosted, signed CRX plus an HTTPS update manifest | admin rights; **not shipped here** |

**Route A is verified, not assumed.** After launching, the plugin asks the debugging port for its raw target list and looks for *this* extension's own worker (`chrome-extension://<id>/background.js`) rather than "some extensio

plugins.description: DSH plugin: prunes the dead streaming fragments out of session logs at startup, so a long session stops expanding into gigabytes when it is loaded. Inert and dry-run by default.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-vacuum

[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-community%20topic-blue)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)
[![deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/deepseek--harness-plugin-4b6bfb)](https://github.com/topics/deepseek-harness)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)

> **Topics:** `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness` · `session-log` · `streaming-fragments` ·
> `vacuum` · `prune` · `oom` · `long-session` · `memory-optimization`

Long DSH sessions get slower and heavier the longer they run. Every load expands the log into
millions of objects, and eventually it OOMs.

Hiding the chunks from the client is not enough: the log on disk is still hundreds of MB, so the
next load rebuilds the same millions of objects and OOMs again. This plugin removes them **at
rest**, so the load itself gets smaller. The session that motivated it was a 1,813-turn
conversation — 224,000 rows, 272 MB on disk, 8.43 million objects on load, 1.29 GB resident,
outcome: OOM.

**You are accumulating this from turn one.** Measured on real sessions, the number of
prunable fragments tracks output tokens at roughly **0.95–0.99 : 1** — eight sessions, from
88 fragments for a 91-token one-turn chat up to 1,498 fragments for a 1,516-token six-turn one.
Nothing reads them; they are write-only.

- **Live by default.** A fresh install prunes idle logs with no configuration at all. Set
  `enabled: false` to switch it off, or `dryRun: true` to watch without writing.
- **Never touches a session written in the last 2 minutes** (`liveWindowMs`).
- **Verified before it writes.** The pruned log has to satisfy the loader contract, or the
  original file is left exactly as it was.
- **Destructive by design.** The fragment rows are **deleted**. `.orig` is the only backup,
  and it is never removed for you. Read [Destructive by design](#destructive-by-design)
  before enabling it.

**Why not just hide the chunks?** Folding them out of the `session.history` response is a real
fix for the client, and this plugin does not replace it — the two run together. But the OOM does
not happen in the client. It happens when DSH loads the log: the file is read, every row is
parsed, and the chunk rows expand into millions of objects. If the file on disk is still 272 MB,
skipping them in the response does not stop the next load from rebuilding them. The only way to
stop that is to make the file smaller — see
[How this differs from the runtime approaches](#how-this-differs-from-the-runtime-approaches).

---

## Why

A session log is a concatenation of zstd frames holding JSONL rows. Every token a model
streams is written twice: once as a raw delta (`assistant/chunk`, and the packed rows
`text-chunks` / `reasoning-chunks` / `tool-call-chunks`) and once inside the finalised
`assistant/message`. **Nothing reads the fragments.** Replay does not read them, the model is
never fed them — the projection layer does not even know the word `chunks`. They accumulate
because they are write-only.

Measured on the session that motivated this plugin, a 1,813-turn conversation:

| | |
|---|---|
| rows in the log | 224,000 |
| file on disk | 272 MB |
| objects after loading it | 8.43 million |
| resident memory while loaded | 1.29 GB |
| outcome | out of memory |

The file is small enough to sit on disk unnoticed and large enough to kill the process that
loads it. And because every load pays that cost, the session gets slower and eventually
unopenable — while the rows that cause it are provably unused.

After a cleanup, on the very same session:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| session file | 86.67 MB | 16.99 MB |
| fragment rows | 169,795 | 0 |
| non-fragment content | — | **nothing lost** (`dropped=0`) |
| generation speed shown by the UI | visibly slow | **back to normal** |

> ⚠️ **The "generation speed" row is an observation, not a promise, and it is not explained.** ✗
> What was observed: after the fragments were removed and load memory dropped, the generation
> speed reported by the UI recovered. No controlled before/after tok/s reading was taken, so
> this records the symptom only. Do not read a mechanism into it: context size, cache hit rate,
> time of day and the reasoning-effort setting were each suspected and each ruled out by data,
> and this is the only thing that was actually confirmed.

## What it does

`startDelayMs` after boot, once:

1. **Scan.** Walk `$DSH_HOME/sessions` for `session.jsonl.zstd`, sort by size, biggest first.
   A file modified inside `liveWindowMs` is `skipped-live` — the plugin never swaps a log
   out from under a session that may be writing to it.
2. **Threshold.** Count fragment rows and their share of all event rows. Below `minChunkRows`
   or below `minRatio`, the file is `below-threshold` and is not touched at all. A few
   hundred kilobytes of fragments is not worth rewriting a log for.
3. **Prune.** Delete the fragment rows, then renumber `seq` and **remap every cross-event
   reference** onto the new numbering — `sourceEventSeqs`, `surfaceOp.start/end`,
   `shadowedSeqs` and `data.shadowedRange`. Events that the remap itself invalidates (a
   `surfaceOp` whose endpoints were dropped, a surface event left without a marker) are
   dropped too, in a fixpoint loop, so the result is consistent rather than almost-consistent.
4. **Self-verify.** The pruned log must satisfy the same contract DSH loads by: contiguous
   `seq` from 0, a marker on every surface event, no dangling references and no reference to
   a later event. Any violation ⇒ `verify-failed` ⇒ **nothing is written** and the log keeps
   its original size. Refusing to shrink a file is always acceptable; writing a file that DSH
   cannot load is not.
5. **Replace atomically.** Copy the original to `<log>.orig` (only if it does not already
   exist), write the new bytes to `<log>.vacuum-tmp`, then `rename` it over the log. A crash
   mid-write leaves the original intact.

The plugin cannot shrink an already-loaded session — it does not need to. Pruning the file
means every *future* load is small, which is where the memory, the stutter and the OOM came
from.

## Running it on demand

The boot run has one practical flaw: it skips anything written inside `liveWindowMs`
(2 minutes by default), which is usually *the session you actually care about*. And until
this interface existed, the run reported only how many files it handled, so a scan that
skipped 56 of 58 logs looked identical to a plugin that does nothing.

Two things follow from that, and both are now in place.

### The log says why every file was skipped

`run-end` carries a count per reason, next to the `handled` it always had:

```json
{"mark":"run-end","scanned":58,"handled":2,"vacuumed":2,"wouldVacuum":0,
 "skippedLive":56,"belowThreshold":0,"unreadable":0,"other":0}
```

`handled` keeps exactly the meaning it always had — the files this run actually acted on.
The rest are the ones it did **not** act on, broken down by the same `status` strings the
`file` lines use. **Nothing about what gets cleaned changed**; this is observability only.

### `clean_session_logs` — ask for a pass now

An agent can call the Host tool **`clean_session_logs`**. It takes no required arguments and
one optional one:

| argument | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dryRun` | `false` | `true` ⇒ preview only: decode, prune and verify every candidate, report what a real pass would save, and write nothing. |

It runs the **same** guarded pass as the boot timer — the same `liveWindowMs` window, the same
two thresholds, the same `vacuumOne()` that backs up to `.orig`, verifies, and replaces
atomically. The on-demand entry point is not a bigger hammer; it just does not have to wait
for the next boot.

It returns **plain text**, not JSON, so what you see in the transcript is what happened:

```
session-vacuum: DRY RUN - nothing was written.
Scanned 4 session log(s) under /home/you/.dsh/sessions.
Would clean: 2 log(s).
  - /home/you/.dsh/sessions/third/session.jsonl.zstd: 0.01 MB -> 0 MB (saves 0.01 MB), 120 fragment row(s) dropped, 92 event(s) kept
  - /home/you/.dsh/sessions/stale/session.jsonl.zstd: 0.01 MB -> 0 MB

plugins.description: Codex-style Create Workspace dialog for DeepSeek Harness: type a name and the folder is created for you, or pick a folder with a native chooser that remembers where you were.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-create-dialog

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Create Workspace** dialog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a name and go, or pick a folder with a chooser that finally remembers where you were.

![The Create Workspace dialog: a name field, a workspace folder row with a Choose folder button, and a New workspace location row with a Change button](docs/create-workspace.png)

## What it does

Clicking **Add workspace…** in DSH today opens the OS folder dialog immediately. This plugin replaces that with a small dialog that asks two independent questions: what is the workspace called, and where does it live. Answer the first only and it creates the folder for you; answer the second and the folder you picked *is* the workspace.

| You do | You get |
| --- | --- |
| Type a name, press **Create** | A new folder with that name is created under **New workspace location**, registered as a workspace, and a session opens in it |
| Click **Choose folder…** | The native Windows folder dialog, starting **where you left off**, not at some default |
| Choose a folder, leave the name empty | The name fills itself in from the folder's own name |
| Choose a folder, having typed a name | Your name wins — the workspace is registered, then renamed to it |
| Click **Change…** on New workspace location | Pick where name-only workspaces go from now on; the choice is saved and survives restarts |
| Cancel / Esc / click the backdrop | Nothing happens — no folder, no registration |

### The effect, before and after

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating `my-project` | Create the folder in Explorer first, then hunt for it in the picker | Type `my-project`. Done |
| The folder picker's starting point | The OS default, every single time | The directory you last chose |
| Where new workspaces land | Wherever you navigate to | A location you set once, visible in the dialog, changeable any time |
| Naming a workspace after its folder | Retype the folder name | Auto-filled |

## Install

### From the DSH UI (simplest)

Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, paste this address, click **Install**, then **Enable now**:

```text
https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
```

That box takes a package name, a Git address, a tarball or a local absolute path. A repository URL works because this package ships a `dsh.bundle` patch — DSH checks exactly that before it installs. Restart DeepSeek Harness if the plugin does not come up.

Two things worth knowing: it downloads straight from GitHub, so GitHub has to be reachable (the China-mirror option only covers registry packages, not repository downloads); and DSH does not auto-update third-party plugins yet — upgrading means uninstall + install again.

> Already installed with `tools/install.mjs` below? Run `node tools/install.mjs --uninstall` first, so the profile does not end up with two loader rows for the same id.

### One-line prompt for your agent

If you would rather not click through it:

```text
Install the DSH plugin at https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog into my DSH and tell me when to restart.
```

### From the plugin market (once listed)

Search for **dsh-workspace-create-dialog** in [dshmarket](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) and install it in one click. The listing is [pending a PR](contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/) to [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) (their CI requires the repository to be at least one day old); until it lands, use the routes above and below.

### Manual install from this repository

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
cd dsh-workspace-create-dialog
node tools/install.mjs
```

That copies the package into your DSH profile's `node_modules` and appends one loader line to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. It resolves your DSH home the same way the harness does — explicit config, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh`.

**Then restart DeepSeek Harness** (the host half is a Node module, so a config reload alone will not import it). After that, changing `lib/client.js` only needs a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` still needs a restart.

`node tools/install.mjs --dry-run` prints what it would do without writing anything; `--uninstall` removes the package and its loader row again.

Publishing to npm is **not** required: the market installs from GitHub exactly the same way, and listing is unaffected either way.

## How it works

### It uses the official extension point, not a patch

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` declares a `single` slot where the "pick a directory" step is handed to whichever plugin fills it:

```text
sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow              ← the sidebar's "Add workspace…"
conversation.hero.workspace.directoryFlow     ← the empty-state entry
```

The owner hands the occupant the whole interaction contract:

```ts
interface DirectoryFlowOwnerProps {
  open: boolean                     // a pick is requested
  busy: boolean                     // the owner is adopting the picked path
  onPicked: (path: string) => void  // report the directory; the owner registers it and opens a session
  onCancel: () => void
  onError: (message: string) => void
}
```

This plugin registers its own occupant into both slots at **priority -100**. A `single` slot renders the lowest-priority entry, the shipped native driver sits at `0`, so this dialog wins (two entries at the *same* priority throw, which is the official protection against ambiguity). Removing the loader line from your profile patch restores the stock behaviour exactly.

### Why the folder dialog is built here instead of reused

The desktop app opens its folder dialog from the Electron main process without a starting directory:

```js
// D:\App\DSH\resources\app.asar → lib/main.js
dialog.showOpenDialog(window, { properties: ['openDirectory', 'createDirectory'] })
```

There is no `defaultPath`, which is exactly why the chooser always starts in the same place. A plugin cannot reach that call: the DSH host is a *child process* of Electron. So `lib/pick-folder.js` opens its own `IFileDialog` — a small C# COM interop compiled and run by the **Windows PowerShell 5.1 that ships with Windows**:

- **no dependencies**: no koffi, no PowerShell 7, no native module to publish;
- compilation happens **in memory** (~120 ms per call), so there is no DLL cache to corrupt or lock;
- the one line that matters is `IFileDialog::SetFolder` — the remembered directory as the starting point;
- the dialog runs in a child process, so a native fault cannot take the host down.

The C# method declaration order must match the COM vtable (`Show=3`, `SetOptions=9`, `SetFolder=12`, `SetTitle=17`, `GetResult=20`). Getting it wrong does not error — it just silently does the wrong thing — so a self-test asserts the order.

## Where name-only workspaces are created

The **New workspace location** is resolved in this order (`lib/base-dir.js`, a pure function):

1. **What you set in the dialog** — highest priority; once you change it, it is yours;
2. **`config.baseDir`** from your profile patch — the value used at install time;
3. **The root of your default workspace** — the parent of the workspace whose directory is named `default-workspace` (a name the harness fixes, independent of UI language). New workspaces land next to it. This is the default for a fresh install;
4. **Fallback** — `<Documents>/deepseek-harness`, or `<home>/deepseek-harness` when there is no Documents folder.

The resolved value is written to the state file, so "what it was on first run" is decided once and only you change it afterwards. `config.baseDir` is a seed, not an order.

## HTTP routes

All four are loopback-guarded (loopback socket + loopback `Host` + same-origin marker; `x-forwarded-for` is never trusted) — they create directories and open windows on the host machine, so nothing off-machine may reach them.

| Route | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/config` | GET | Current location + last directory |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/base-dir` | POST | `{"

plugins.description: GitMate — a smart Git panel for DeepSeek Harness: diffs, generated commit messages, a commit graph with rewind, and .gitignore generation, plus ten agent tools.
plugins.readme_text:
# GitMate

**A Git panel in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) sidebar — plus the same operations as fifteen agent tools.**

Runs anywhere the Harness does: macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell).

Only two things genuinely differ across platforms, and both live on the Host side: **how arguments are quoted** (PowerShell doubles a single quote, a POSIX shell closes-escapes-reopens; chosen by `process.platform`) and **how the environment is passed** (through the shell request's `env` field rather than a POSIX `VAR=value` prefix, which is not a command on Windows). Nothing else is platform-aware: paths go through `node:path`, nothing outside `lib/` is written, and no file needing an executable bit is created. When the sandbox will not start, the advice **names the cause for the platform you are on** (bubblewrap/Landlock on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `%TEMP%` on Windows).

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Review changes, read diffs, stage, commit with a generated message, merge, stash, sync, and rewind history without leaving the panel. Every operation is also a tool the agent can call, so asking in chat works too.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:alanhaskey/dsh-gitmate
```

Restart DSH once, refresh the page, then open **GitMate** from the sidebar's **+** menu.

> The internal ids (Loader row `dsh-git`, tab key) differ from the package name on purpose: the row id is the key of a config row you may already have, and renaming it would orphan your saved settings.

## Reviewing and committing

- **Four groups** — conflicts, staged, changes, untracked. Each row shows the kind in words, the path, and that file's `+N −M`. Row actions stage, unstage, and discard, with a second click for anything destructive.
- **Diffs like an editor** — two line-number gutters, `+`/`−` markers, tinted rows, and only the changed span of a replaced line marked. Click a file to expand it in place; click again to collapse. Widen the context from 3 lines to 24 when a hunk needs more of the file.
- **One row of list actions**, shown only when they would do something, with the counts in the labels.
- **Amend** — fold the staged changes into the previous commit; leaving the message box empty keeps the existing message.
- **A draggable splitter** between the list and the commit card resizes the message box.
- **A panel that is working says so** — every operation shows a turning indicator and names itself ("Committing…", "Reviewing the staged changes…") instead of only greying its buttons out. It sits with the messages at the foot of the list, above the splitter, so it never covers the commit box.

## AI features

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Commit message** | Generated from the staged diff. If you have already typed something, the button becomes *Refine draft*: the model keeps your intent and fills in the rest instead of replacing it. |
| **Review before commit** | Reads the staged changes and reports only what would bite — a wrong result, a missed edge case, an unhandled error, a committed secret, debug output left in, a behaviour change with no test. Click a finding to open that file's diff. |
| **Split this commit** | Divides the staged changes into commits that each stand on their own, with a message for each. The plan is a draft you can edit: rewrite any message, merge a group into the one above, remove one, ask for a new plan, commit one group at a time, or commit them all in order. Each commit leaves the other files staged. |
| **Explain a change** | Two to five bullets on what a file's change does, so you can review without reading every line. |
| **`.gitignore`** | Infers the rules from the project's manifests and layout. One button creates it; one adds what is missing **and tidies the whole file** — exact duplicates, rules an earlier broader rule already covers (`node_modules/.cache/` after `node_modules/`), and runs of blank lines. It groups entries under headings only when that cannot change the meaning: with a `!` rule (git decides by the last match, so order is semantic) or with your own comments, the order is kept and the panel says so. |

Buttons that call a model are marked **AI**. Every generation uses the session's default model — there is no second model to configure.

## Branches, history, remotes

- **Branch selector** — switch, create, delete, and merge any branch into the checked-out one. A conflicted merge is reported with the files that need a decision, and can be aborted.
- **Commit graph** — every branch and remote-tracking branch, not just this one. Expand a commit for its full message, the files it touched, and what you can do to it: rewind, revert, cherry-pick, rebase, or tag. Click a changed file to see its diff inside that commit.
- **Remotes** — push, pull, fetch, and a **Sync** that fetches, fast-forwards, then pushes. It refuses to merge a diverged branch rather than inventing a merge commit.
- **Stash** — set work aside and take it back later (pop, apply, drop).

## Setup

Without a repository the **history button is disabled** — there is no history to show — while **settings stays reachable**, because that is where someone looks when the panel is not doing what they expect. If the repository disappears while the panel is open (the folder changed, `.git` was removed), the view falls back to the change list rather than leaving the button lit on a view that cannot render.



One click initialises a repository and writes the local commit identity; two buttons handle `.gitignore`. Nothing is chosen from a list of ecosystems — the plugin reads the project and decides.

## Configuration

Settings live in this plugin's own row in `cordis.patch.yml`, so they survive upgrades and stay visible on the Plugins page. Everything below is a button or a checkbox; there is nothing to type unless you want custom instructions.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageLanguage` | `auto` | Language of generated text: `auto` (follow the repository), `en`, `zh`. When unset or `auto`, the panel's own messages read as Chinese. |
| `messageStyle` | `conventional` | `conventional` (`feat: …`) or `plain`. |
| `messageTemplate` | — | Extra instructions, appended last so they override the defaults. |
| `signoff` | `false` | Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer. |
| `defaultBranch` | `main` | Branch created by *Initialise*. |
| `maxPromptBytes` | `24000` | Diff text handed to the model per change set. |
| `maxDiffBytes` | `80000` | Patch text a tool returns before truncating. |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per git command; network commands get four times this. |

## Safety

- **Nothing destructive happens on a single click.** Discarding, deleting a branch, dropping a stash, rebasing, and rewinding all ask first, and say what will be lost.
- **Rewinding and reverting are separate**, because they are: rewinding moves the branch and rewrites history, reverting adds an inverse commit and is safe for anything already pushed. The panel warns before a rewind that would rewrite published history.
- **"Undo this commit" and "rewind to here" are separate too.** On the newest commit the button undoes that commit and leaves its changes staged, unstaged, or deleted as you choose; on an older commit it moves the branch pointer back to that commit. The notice names the commit that was actually undone and always states how many were discarded — including none.
- **A refusal says which mode refused.** A read-only session cannot write `.git`, so committing and switching branches are rejected by design; the message names the mode and what to switch to. If it is already `danger-full-access` and still refused, the sandbox backend on that machine is refusing writes and the Harness needs restarting — two different problems, told apart.
- **git's own diagnostics are pinned to English** (`LC_ALL=C`). The plugin's text is still localised by the setting; git's is kept stable because the phrase table in `lib/text.js` matches English sentences, and a localised git defeats it — worse on Windows, where git writes in the console code page and the pipeline decodes UTF-8, so a Chinese message arrives as mojibake.
- **The

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lock

给 DSH（DeepSeek Harness）网页版加一道**密码门禁**：打开页面先显示锁定界面，输入密码解锁后才能使用。

## 功能

- **全屏遮罩**：未解锁时覆盖整个界面，阻止直接操作会话
- **手动锁定**：随时一键锁定（侧边栏按钮 + 快捷键）
- **自动锁定**：可配置空闲时长后自动锁定
- **密码安全**：仅存 scrypt 单向哈希，**永不保存明文**
- **界面中英双语**：跟随 DSH 的界面语言设置实时切换（见下方「界面文案（运行时 locale）」）

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:felixpu/dsh-lock
```

安装后重启宿主进程。

## 使用

| 操作 | 方式 |
|---|---|
| 解锁 | 在锁定界面输入密码 |
| 立即锁定 | 侧边栏底部「锁定」按钮 |
| 立即锁定（快捷键） | macOS / Windows：`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + L`；Linux：`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + .` |
| 自动锁定时长 | 设置 → 插件 → dsh-lock |

> Linux 用 `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + .` 而非 `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + L`：DSH 平台的 Linux 键位白名单
> 不接受「修饰键 + 字母」，为各平台分别声明才不会被校验拒绝。

## 配置

本包不导出 `Config` schema，密码与自动锁定设置由插件自身持久化，通过「设置 → 插件 → dsh-lock」面板管理。

## 安全说明

- 密码以 **scrypt**（N=2^15, r=8, p=1）加盐哈希存储，比对使用常量时间比较
- 解锁后签发的是短期令牌，而非保存密码本身
- 存储位置在插件私有目录下，卸载插件不会把密码留在会话或配置里

> ⚠️ 这是**界面门禁**，不是磁盘加密。它防的是「别人走到你电脑前直接操作 DSH」，
> 不能防止能读取你用户目录下文件的攻击者。

## 宿主贡献

- `inject: ['webServer']`，注册解锁/锁定相关的同源路由
- 无客户端以外的外部依赖
- **不产出面向用户的自然语言**：所有路由响应只回机器可读的 `error` code
  （如 `invalid-password` / `too-many-attempts` / `locked`），由客户端字典翻译。
  宿主无从知道 UI 语言，写死中/英文都会在另一种语言下露馅。
  唯一保留自然语言的地方是宿主**日志**（`ctx.logger.info`），那是给开发者看的。

## 界面文案（运行时 locale）

界面文案走**平台官方 locale 服务**，中英双语：

```js
// client/client.js
inject: ['slots', 'shortcuts', 'locale'],
apply(ctx) {
  ctx.effect(() => ctx.locale.register(NS, { zh, en }), NS + ': dictionaries');
  const t = ctx.locale.bind(NS);
  ctx.slots.register({ name: 'shell.overlay', id: '…', locale: NS }, Veil); // ← 渲染器据此注入 t
}
```

组件从 `props.t` 拿翻译函数，**不需要**自己 `inject: () => ({ t })` ——
槽注册选项里给了 `locale: NS`，渲染器（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` 的
`standardKit()`）会把绑定好的 `t` 注入 props；缺 locale 插件时它会抛出明确的
`SlotAssemblyError`，而不是静默渲染出 key 名。

约定：

- 一条消息 = 一个完整句子，变量用 `{name}` 占位（如 `'autoLock.minutes': '{n} 分钟'` /
  `'{n} minutes'`）。**不拆片段拼接**，否则中英语序无法重排。
- 键名小写点分层级：`lock.title`、`field.password`、`button.unlock`、
  `error.wrongPassword`、`autoLock.minutes`。
- `retry` / `loading` / `unknown` 等平台 `common` 命名空间已有的通用词**不重复定义**，
  查表未命中会自动回落到 common。
- **zh 与 en 的键必须完全一致**：运行时不校验，漏键只会显示 key 名。故 `apply` 里
  做了一次键一致性自查，不一致时 `console.warn` 点名缺的键。
- 需要本地化的字符串**不能**只存在于源码字面量里 —— 静态审计
  （去掉注释后 grep 中文字符）应只剩注释与宿主日志。

## 展示元数据（locale）

`locale/en.json` 与 `locale/zh.json` 提供**插件展示元数据**（`meta.title` / `meta.description`），
Plugin Manager 与设置页**无需激活插件**即可读取，用于显示本地化的插件名与说明。
这与运行时 UI 文案（客户端 `ctx.locale.register`，见上一节）是**两套互不相关**的东西：
前者是 JSON 资源、由宿主按 Node 模块解析器读取；后者是客户端代码里的字典对象。

```json
{ "meta": { "title": "…", "description": "…" } }
```

⚠️ 两个容易漏的点（漏任一个都会**静默失效**，不报错）：

1. **必须在 `package.json` 的 `exports` 里导出 `./locale/*.json`** —— 宿主经 Node 模块解析器
   读取该资源，未导出的子路径会得到 `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`，被当作「没有 locale」跳过。
2. **`files` 需包含 `locale`** —— 否则 `pnpm pack` / `npm publish` 的产物里不会带上它。

`icon.svg` 走顶层 `icon` 字段（相对路径），**不需要** `exports`。

## 客户端挂载点

| 槽位 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| 全屏遮罩 | 未解锁时的锁定界面 |
| `sidebar.footer.action` | 「立即锁定」按钮 |
| `plugins.bundle.config` | 自动锁定设置面板 |

客户端 bundle 仅 `require` 平台种子表内的模块（本包只用到 `react`）。
槽位 / 快捷键 / 语言三个服务通过 `package.json` 的 `dsh.client.inject` 声明，
在插件对象 `inject: ['slots', 'shortcuts', 'locale']` 里注入 —— 服务不走 `require`。

快捷键的 `label` 用**函数**（thunk）而非字符串，语言切换后快捷键面板那一行会跟着变；
`aliases` 是快捷键面板的**搜索别名**、平台没有本地化机制，故只放英文
（官方各包一律如此），写死中文会让英文界面下露出中文。

## 许可证

MIT © felixpu

## 仓库

<https://github.com/felixpu/dsh-lock>

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-our-free-model **简体中文** | [English](README_EN.md)
> 你只需在 dsh 里装上这个插件，无需登录、注册、填 API Key 或任何其它操作， > 就能用上包括 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3 在内的前沿模型——完全免费，不限量。 > > *All you do is install this plugin in dsh: no login, no sign-up, no API key, nothing > else. The frontier models are just there — DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3 and the rest. > Free, with no usage cap.* > > 模型清单跟随上游刷新，可用性由**你自己这台机器的网络出口**实测得出， > 思考强度下发的是真实预算而不是提示词，另附一个 OpenAI 兼容的本地转发端口。 > > 纯插件挂载：不改内核、无构建步骤、零依赖。
--- ## 交流群

QQ 群：386179533（AI 技术交流学习群）
扫码加入群聊，一起交流插件使用心得、反馈问题与分享玩法。
--- ## 亮点 - **开箱即用，无配置环节**——不需要账号、不需要 Key、不需要在后台申请配额。 - **上游来源公开透明**——免费车道来源为 OpenCode 的 Zen 网关（https://opencode.ai），Kilo 渠道来源为 Kilo AI 的公共网关（https://kilo.ai），均直连、不经任何第三方中转。请求由谁处理、数据发往何处，见「上游是哪些源」与「免责声明」。 - **清单跟随上游**——模型集合、上下文长度与能力在每次刷新时向上游重新拉取，插件内不保存静态快照。 - **选择器只广播可用的模型**——上游清单已声明但网关明确拒绝路由的模型（返回 `Model is unavailable`、或 404 找不到该 id）从下拉框移除，仅在设置页保留记录并注明拒因；网关自身故障（5xx）、配额限制（429）、超时与断网不属于对模型的判定，一律保持可达；被地区策略拦截的模型归入 region-limited 分组。整轮探测全部被拒时同样保留，选择器不会为空。 - **公告中心 + 实时推送**——仓库维护者在仓库中编辑 JSON 并推送后，所有已安装实例最迟在一个轮询周期内收到；正文为白名单约束下的 HTML，支持图文排版；`urgent` 级别触发全屏弹窗；可选系统级通知。 - **应用内升级**——设置页一键升级：下载 → SHA-256 校验 → 备份 → 原子替换 → 校验回读 → 热重载，任一步失败自动回滚至上一版本。 - **热重载**——升级与代码变更即时生效，无需重启应用；也可在设置页手动触发，或启用文件监视自动重载。 - **按响应体形状判定流式响应**——网关在高负载下会以 `application/json` 的 content-type 返回完整的 SSE 帧序列。插件按响应体形状判定，并将已嗅探的字节重新注入流，既不会导致整轮失败，也不会因 header 与实际内容不符而将可用模型判为不可用。 - **思考强度实际生效**——Light / Balanced / Deep 对应输出 token 预算 2 048 / 8 192 / 模型上限，且逐次调用留痕。思考不可关闭的模型（MiMo V2.6 等）三档整体翻倍为 4 096 / 16 384 / 模型上限，因为思考与正文共享同一输出额度；设置页每张模型卡均标注该档位实际下发的上限。该能力通过硬性输出上限实现，不依赖上游的 effort 参数（原因见「为什么用预算，而不是 reasoning_effort」）。 - **不依赖浏览器界面**——插件仅将 llm 作为硬依赖，在没有 web server 的 composition（如 dsh-tui）中同样完成启动并输出模型；看板模块挂载在独立的 fiber 上，待 webServer 就绪后再注册路由，因此既不会阻塞模型车道，也不会因插件先于 web 服务加载而永久丢失设置页。 - **用量看板，数据全部留在本机**——Token 热力图、总量曲线（支持总计与单模型视图）、输出速度与首字延迟逐次采样。不上传任何数据。 - **OpenAI 兼容转发端口**——本机其它工具通过 base URL 与 Key 即可调用这些模型。 - **EAC 渠道（桌面端专属）**——在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端与 DSHEAC AIO 桌面端中自动解锁一条协付通道，模型以 EAC 前缀显示（如 EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash）；凭据加密密封，由宿主指纹闸门把守；该渠道在服务器侧校验 GitHub 授权（登录并 star 本仓库）后才放行对话；在命令行及其它宿主中该通道完全不存在。详见「EAC 渠道」。 - **Kilo 渠道（免密免费池）**——内置 Kilo AI 公共网关的免费模型池（`isFree` 清单实时拉取，含 `kilo-auto/free` 自动路由），无需任何账号或 Key；模型卡带 Kilo 徽章。思考强度与 EAC 渠道同款：模型自身的档位菜单（Off / Low / Medium / High，默认 High），经网关统一的 `reasoning` 参数真实下发——Off 已逐家族实测将思考归零（nemotron、ling、dots、poolside、apodex、cohere）；stepfun 与 liquid 端点强制思考（对关闭请求返回 400）、两个自动路由不透传关闭，这些模型的菜单不含 Off 档。该池由上游免费提供，上游会在其模型卡中声明 prompt 可能被记录用于改进服务——请勿发送敏感内容，详见「免责声明」。 - **聚合渠道，自带 Key**——设置页新增一页，把第三方端点接进同一条模型清单：注册表内置 76 家提供商（NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter、Groq、Cerebras、SambaNova、Gemini、DeepSeek、Mistral、Together、Fireworks、SiliconFlow、Nebius、Chutes、Hugging Face、Cloudflare、Z.ai、Kimi、MiniMax、QwenCloud/Alibaba、Bedrock、Vertex、Vercel AI Gateway、Azure OpenAI，以及无需账号的 Ollama、LM Studio、llama.cpp），写入 Key（本机免账号的提供商不需要）后其模型即以 `provider/model` 出现在选择器里，也可经本地网关调用。Key 只写入本机 0600 的 settings.json，API 只回显 `hasKey` 与 `…abcd` 指纹；每家可单独启停、测试（列表探测，不花一次生成）、发现模型、覆盖 Base URL 与模型清单。OAuth 与 ADC 认证的提供商照常列出，但标注为不可驱动。 - **省 Token**——三件事：工具输出压缩（RTK）在请求发出前就地重写 `tool_result`（git diff / status / log、grep、find、ls、tree、构建日志、编号转储、搜索清单、重复日志行），实测 40 KB 的 `git diff` 移除 90% 的字节且模型仍能就它作答；提示词瘦身有 caveman 与 ponytail 两族、默认全关；另有五个不占用上游请求的本地应答。设置页用与用量图表同一批统计行显示压缩前后字节、节省比例、压缩块数与统计调用数。 - **路由（降级链）**——把任意车道的模型串成一条命名链，以 `combo:` 作为虚拟模型出现在选择器与网关上；`fallback` 固定从链首开始，`round-robin` 轮换起点并连续 N 轮粘滞。链接在输出任何正文之前失败会被整段丢弃，切换对调用方不可见；思考增量不算正文，因此「想了很久才撞上配额墙」正是降级最有价值的场景。 - **本地网关原生说 Anthropic**——新增 `POST /v1/messages`（流式与非流式，含 thinking / tool_use 块、真实 stop_reason 与流内 error 事件）与 `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`（本地估算）；`/v1/models` 广播全部车道，含聚合行与链路。网关页新增「接入客户端」分区，按实际绑定的端口与真实要求的密钥生成 Claude Code、Codex、OpenAI SDK、Anthropic SDK、curl 与局域网的可复制配方。 - **接口具备鉴权围栏**——插件 HTTP 路由优先级高于内核 `/api`，因此内置与内核一致的信任检查（优先复用 composition 的 connection 服务，缺失时退回结构化围栏）。 - **十三个白嫖渠道，一体接入**——CodeArts（华为云）、CodeBuddy / WorkBuddy（腾讯）、LobsterAI（有道）、Qoder / Qoder 中国版（阿里系）、TRAE（字节）、Cline、Loomy（讯飞）、Raccoon（商汤）、MiniMax Code、ZCode（智谱）、Gemini（Google Code Assist）十一个账号渠道开箱即用，外加 Kilo 免费车道与原匿名免费通道；OpenCode 账号渠道在本插件中默认停用。各渠道的登录流程、账号池、每日积分领取、模型黑名单与其本地 OpenAI 网关（Chat Completions + Responses，默认 `127.0.0.1:8326`）原样挂载与运行；凭据只写入宿主凭据库，浏览器永远拿不到明文。 - **九页毛玻璃界面**——设置页顶部导航扩为九个页面：原有六页（**免费模型**（鱼缸水位 = 可用模型占比）、**EAC 模型**（鱼缸水位 = 协付池压力）、**白嫖模型接入**（十三张渠道卡：登录、账号、模型开关、一键领取积分）、**数据看板**（今日/全部 Token 消耗、平均生成速度、缓存命中率、成功率，账号透视与模型性能表、最近请求总览）、**运行日志**（逐请求明细：结果、耗时、首字、速度、Token 细分，失败原因悬停可见）与**网关设置**（网关开关/端点/密钥；局域网转发中继：监听地址、端口与独立中继密钥）），新增**聚合渠道**（提供商注册表、Key、测试、发现模型、Base URL 与模型清单覆盖）、**省 Token**（压缩开关、两族提示词档位、五个本地应答与节省统计）与**路由**（降级链编辑器）三页；网关设置页另增「接入客户端」分区。页面切换与卡片入场为 150–250 ms 短动效，`prefers-reduced-motion` 下整体关闭。每页都有直达 GitHub 仓库的 Star 按钮。 - **局域网转发中继**——渠道网关本身只监听本机（上游的安全选择）；本插件提供自己的转发门：调用方用插件签发与轮换的中继密钥，转发跳由宿主换用网关凭据（凭据不出宿主进程），仅放行 `/v1/*` 模型接口并带环路保护。 ## 你会看到什么 **输入框的模型选择器** | 分组 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | Our Free Model | 当前网络出口可直接使用的模型 | | Our Free Model · region-limited | 上游对该地区不放行的模型，保留可见但单独隔离 | 被判定为「已声明但不路由」的模型不出现在任何分组中——它们仅在设置页的「不在选择器中」分组保留记录， 附带拒因与探测时间；后续探测重新通过后自动回到选择器。 **设置页** 设置 → Our Free Model，包含七个分区： - **模型清单**——各模型的可用性、是否支持视觉、上下文窗口、最长输出、各思考档位实际下发的输出上限、实测首字延迟，以及单次调用基准测试按钮。 - **EAC 渠道授权**——一键发起 GitHub 登录（自动打开浏览器，无需复制粘贴）、显示登录名与 star 校验状态、重新检查、退出登录；未授权时模型卡带锁标记。免费车道的模型不受影响。 - **公告中心**——仓库维护者推送的公告流：未读计数、紧急徽章、单条/全部标记已读、检查新公告按钮、系统通知开关。公告正文按白名单渲染 HTML。 - **用量看板**——总览计数、17 周 Token 热力图、总量曲线（Token / 请求数切换，总计与单模型切换）、速度迷你图、按模型汇总表。 - **本地转发**——开关、监听地址与端口、复制 base URL、显示 / 复制 / 轮换 API Key，并提供可直接执行的 curl 示例。 - **插件设置**——总开关、是否展示地区受限模型、探测间隔、默认输出上限，以及当前探测到的出口 IP 与国家。 - **插件升级**——当前/最新版本、检查更新、一键升级（含进度与失败原因）、最近一次升级历史、热重载按钮与文件监视开关。 - **首次启动公告**——分 5 页（前言 / 模型清单 / 使用步骤 / 功能介绍 / 公告与升级），确认一次后不再弹出，除非文案版本号被提升。 ## 独立本地服务（开发中） 仓库现在提供两个入口：下文安装的是 **DSH 插件**；`packages/standalone` 是 **无需安装 DSH 的独立本地服务**。从完整源码仓库运行： ```powershell npm run start:standalone ``` 独立服务默认使用 `~/.our-free-model` 和端口 `18900`，拥有自己的 API Key， 不读取插件数据。支持匿名/Kilo、EAC 和原有十三个账号渠道，提供 Chat Completions、Responses API，以及独立网页管理（模型、统计、渠道、EAC、设置、API Key）。 启动后打开终端打印的一次性管理链接即可使用；账号在独立页面登录，也可手动导入插件账号备份。 启动、参数与验证见 [独立服务说明](packages/standalone/README.md)。 独立服务的安装制品与 Release 尚未发布。 ## 安装 **命令行（纯 dsh web）** ``` dsh plugin --profile web add /绝对路径/dsh-our-free-model ``` 安装完成后重启应用一次。`--profile` 填写实际使用的 profile 名称。 **DSHEAC AIO / 桌面端：请先阅读本节** 桌面端在启动 web 服务之前会执行一道 profile 闸门。其扫描器仅放行 dsh 自身在 .dsh-module-fallback 下生成的链接；profile 目录树中出现任何其它符号链接或目录 junction，应用将拒绝启动并报错： ``` PROFILE_UPGRADE_REQUIRED: offline dependency migration is not yet available ``` 因此桌面端不要使用 `link:` 依赖安装，也不要创建 junction。请使用应用内的插件管理器， 或放置一个真实目录。 以真实目录手工安装时，在 /profiles// 下完成三项操作： 1. 将发布文件复制至 node_modules/dsh-our-free-model/ （index.js、client.js、adapter/、src/、locale/、icon.svg、cordis.patch.yml、package.json——adapter/ 不可遗漏：index.js 首行即 import 该目录） 2. 在 dependencies 中加入 "dsh-our-free-model": "2.1.0"——该版本号跟随仓库 package.json 的 version（版本变更时同步，当前为 2.1.0），不要沿用旧值，也不要写为 link: 3. 在 dsh.profile.bundles 末尾追加 "dsh-our-free-model" 不要再向 cordis.patch.yml 添加条目。被 dsh.profile.bundles 引用的包，其自带的 patch 层会自动生效；两处同时注册将报错 duplicate loader entry id: our-free-model。 **整合包（托管安装）** 插件由整合包（EAC 整合包、Mojobox 等）安装时，更新时机与文件字节由安装方控制： 安装时将 bundle config 设为 distributio

plugins.description: Use the MiniMax Code (Mavis) subscription already signed in on this machine as a DeepSeek Harness model provider — with self-renewing credentials, a points/check-in panel and a model roster editor.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-minimax-connect

把本机 **MiniMax Code（Mavis）** 已登录的订阅接入 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)，作为一个模型 provider，并在设置侧边栏给出一个独立页面：**积分余额 / 每日签到 / 模型清单 / 用量**。

积分制账号：不消耗 API key，消耗 MiniMax Code 订阅的积分。

> **不用打开 MiniMax Code。** 插件自己完成 OAuth 续期，桌面客户端可以完全退出。
> 详见 [凭据自续期](#凭据自续期)。

English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)

---

## 为什么不需要"反代"

MiniMax Code 的推理端点**本身就是 Anthropic Messages 协议**，DSH 的 `pi-ai` 原生支持该协议。所以直接把请求打到官方端点即可，不需要中间代理进程，也不需要 hook 客户端。

`~/.minimax/config.yaml` 里 MiniMax 自己就写着：

```yaml
provider:
  minimax:
    npm: '@ai-sdk/anthropic'
    options:
      baseURL: https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm/v1
```

## 实测契约（全部为真实响应，非推测）

| 用途 | 方法与路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 对话 | `POST {llm}/v1/messages` | Anthropic Messages 协议；流式返回 `thinking_delta` + `text_delta` |
| 模型清单 | — | `GET {llm}/v1/models` 返回 **503 `direct_route_not_configured`**；改从本地 `config.yaml` 静态解析 |
| 续期 | `POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token` | `grant_type=refresh_token`，见下 |
| 积分 | `GET {cloud}/credit/details` | `details[]` 带 `granted_amount` / `remaining_amount` / `consumed_amount` |
| 签到面板 | `GET {cloud}/signin/status?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai` | **`timezone_id` 是必需参数**，缺则 `1406010011 invalid timezone_id` |
| 签到 | `POST {cloud}/signin/claim?timezone_id=Asia/Shanghai`，body `{}` | 空 body 与官方客户端一致；**同样需要 `timezone_id`** |

其中：

```
{llm}   = https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm
{cloud} = https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1
```

**注意两个 base 不同**：Anthropic SDK 会自己在 `baseURL` 后补 `/v1/messages`，所以 `{llm}` **不带**结尾的 `/v1`；而 cloud 路由**带** `/v1`。

## 鉴权

读 `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json`，取 `records[*].accessToken`（`mmoat_` 开头），以 **`Authorization: Bearer`** 发送。

> ⚠️ **不能用 Anthropic 的 `x-api-key`**：实测报 `401 {"code":401,"message":"token is required"}`。

记录键是 `` `${service}\0${account}` ``，分隔符是**真的 NUL 字符**，`account` = `base64url(sha256(authHome + "\0" + "mcode-public"))`。

## 凭据自续期

access token **有效期 1 小时**。MiniMax Code 大致每小时续期一次并写回同一个文件 —— 在它之外没有任何东西会做这件事，所以关掉桌面客户端后，插件在 token 过期的那一刻就废了：实测过期后第一个请求回 `401 invalid access token`，而记录里躺着一个完全可用的 `refreshToken` 无人问津。

本插件自己执行同一个 grant：

```
POST https://account.minimax.cn/oauth2/token
     grant_type=refresh_token
     refresh_token=<mmort_…>
     client_id=mcode-public
     scope=agent.default
     audience=agent-backend
  -> { access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in, scope }
```

行为：

- **提前 5 分钟续期**，不让任何一条流开在一个正在死掉的 token 上。除按需触发外，还有一条 60 秒的巡检。
- **`refresh_token` 单次有效、每次 grant 都轮换**，所以旧值在应答到达的瞬间就死了，新的一对必须在用新 access token 之前落盘。写入是**原子替换**（临时文件 + rename），桌面客户端不会读到写了一半的记录。
- **与官方客户端共存**。客户端用文件锁串行化自己的续期（`proper-lockfile`，`auth.lock` → `auth.lock.lock` 目录，`stale: 30_000`）。这里复用同一套 on-disk 约定：`mkdir` 抢占、超过 30 秒的锁按陈旧回收、写入前重新读一次文件并**采纳更新的 generation 而不是覆盖它**。两边轮流续期互不踢出，已实测双向共存。
- **两个文件必须同步推进**。客户端 `MCodeOAuthCore.readUsableCredential` 要求 `credential.generation === state.generation`，不一致就当成未登录。新代际取 `max(state.generation, credential.generation) + 1` —— 只用凭据自己的计数器，就可能写回一个**低于** `auth-state.json` 的值，把账号锁在自己的新 token 外面。
- **失败不抛异常**，一律回 `{ ok: false, reason, fatal? }`，调用方继续用盘上已有的 token。`fatal` 只标记一种永久失败：`invalid_grant`（refresh token 本身没了），此时只有去 MiniMax Code 重新登录一次能把 provider 救回来。

设一面卡片会直接显示当前状态：*自动续期已启用（到期前 5 分钟），不用打开 MiniMax Code* / *正在自动续期…* / *自动续期暂停，HH:MM:SS 后重试* / *凭据没有 refreshToken，需在 MiniMax Code 里重新登录一次*。

### 端到端验证

`test/renew-e2e.mjs` 只把 `expiresAtMs` 改到"即将过期"（**两个 token 一个都不碰**，所以 grant 失败也是零代价），然后调用插件自己发货的 `renewCredential`，最后拿新 token 打真实模型端点：

```bash
node test/renew-e2e.mjs ~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json
```

在 MiniMax Code **进程数为 0** 的情况下实测通过：grant 273 ms、代际 +1、两个文件代际相等、`loginEpoch` 保留、`refreshToken` 轮换，新 token 打 `/v1/messages` 返回 **HTTP 200** `{"text":"ok","base_resp":{"status_code":0}}`。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "github:VICqiufeeng/dsh-minimax-connect"
```

1. 装在 profile 的 `node_modules` 下，`dsh.profile.bundles` 会自动加上这一项。
2. **重启 DSH** 后生效。
3. 本插件不写用户补丁层（不碰 `cordis.patch.yml`），卸载时从 `dependencies` 与 `dsh.profile.bundles` 两处移除即可，不留残留。

如果 pnpm 的供应链闸门报 `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION`（对 git 依赖一般不触发），追加 `--config.minimumReleaseAge=0`。

## 界面

**设置 → MiniMax**（`settings.section` 插槽，order 460），四个区块：

- **积分 + 签到 + 账号** —— 通用积分余额、七天签到面板、账号信息与续期状态。
- **模型清单** —— 逐模型开关 / 图片输入 / 上下文窗口（200K 或 1M）。
- **保存行** —— 落盘到插件自己的 settings 命名空间 `llm-minimax`。

同一份卡片也会出现在**插件管理页**（侧边栏「插件」图标 → 已安装 → `dsh-minimax-connect`）的详情里，因为它同时注册了 `plugins.bundle.config` 与 `plugins.row.config`。

另有一个自包含的零构建 HTML 面板：`GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel`。

## 路由（全部仅回环）

| 路由 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/status` | 汇总快照（面板用），含 `selfRenewal` |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/usage` | 积分明细原始应答 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/checkin` | 签到状态 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin` | 七天签到面板原始应答 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/signin/claim` | 执行签到 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/models` | 当前模型清单 |
| `POST /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/__save` | 写回启用模型 / 图片开关 / 上下文窗口 |
| `GET /plugins/dsh-minimax-connect/panel` | 自包含 HTML 面板（无构建步骤） |

## 配置

`Config`（schemastery）可覆盖的字段：

| 字段 | 默认 |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/mavis/api/v1/llm` |
| `cloudBaseUrl` | `https://agent.minimax.cn/minimax-cloud/api/v1` |
| `authFile` | `~/.minimax/auth/prod/cn/mcode-public/auth.json` |
| `configFile` | `~/.minimax/config.yaml` |
| `cacheMs` | `15000` |
| `enabledModelIds` / `imageOverrides` / `useMaximumContextWindow` | 由设置页写入 |
| 各 `*Route` | 见上表 |

## 模型

清单来自本地 `~/.minimax/config.yaml` 的 `whitelist` + `model_order`，默认四个：

| 模型 | 上下文 | 图片 | 推理 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MiniMax-M3` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 可开关 |
| `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` | 512K / 1M | ✅ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |
| `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` | 200K | ❌ | 强制 |

## 已知限制

- **积分不换算成本**：模型描述符的 `cost` 全为 0。积分制下没有公开的每 token 单价，填 0 好过填一个编出来的数字。
- **依赖客户端非公开接口**：MiniMax 更新后端点可能变动；端点集中在 `lib/index.js` 顶部注释里，便于对照。
- **图片输入**走宿主的 durable attachment service。老版本宿主不提供该服务时会回 `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT`，插件对两种 store 形状都做了适配。
- 只测过 **Windows + 国内版（cn）**。区域路径与 `buildEnv` 硬编码在 `defaultAuthFile()` 里，其它区域需要改这一处。

## 设计说明

代码里凡是"为什么这么写"的地方都留了注释，几处值得一读的：

- `credential renewal` 段头：为什么插件不得不接管续期。
- `mirrorAuthState` / `nextGeneration`：两个文件代际必须一致的原因，以及那个会导致锁死自己的 off-by-one。
- `withAuthLock`：为什么复刻 `proper-lockfile` 的 on-disk 约定而不是依赖它。
- `adaptAttachmentStore`：宿主 attachment store 的两种形状。

## License

plugins.readme_text:
WTQ账号池

把本机已登录的 WorkBuddy、Trae、Qoder 账号接入 DeepSeek Harness，限流或额度用尽时自动换号。

English | 简体中文

安装 · 功能 · 设置 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

把本机 WorkBuddy、Trae、Qoder 的桌面登录接入 DeepSeek Harness。WorkBuddy 被限流或额度用尽时自动换号；Trae、Qoder 按请求选择账号，不保证失败后重试。三个来源独立开关，国内与国际账号分别成组。 ## 预览 设置面板界面如下（默认亮色）： ![账号池](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-pool.png) 面板载入时读取 DeepSeek Harness 的外观设置；宿主切换主题后须重新载入面板： ![暗色主题](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-dark.png) 模型页可以改显示名、上下文窗口、输出上限、思考等级和贴图。Trae 目录给出费率的模型会带上 `x0.79` 这样的费率标签，未给出费率的模型（以及 Qoder 全部模型）不标注： ![模型设置](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-models.png) 在线预览：。 `docs/index.html` 加载实际面板代码并使用虚构演示数据，支持来源切换、模型设置和主题预览，不读取本机账号或令牌。 ![预览页](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-page.png) 开启 `showComposerPoints` 后，输入区显示当前模型的账号积分，点击可查看该组账号并切换账号。下图由实际输入框扩展离屏渲染，非对话测试截图： ![输入框积分](https://github.com/chengzhi-c/dsh-wtq-pool/raw/main/docs/preview-composer.png) 本地预览需先克隆仓库，再运行 `node docs/serve.cjs` 并打开它输出的地址。该页面不能用 `file://` 打开，浏览器不允许它读取同目录的面板文件。 ## 功能 - 复用本机登录：只读三家桌面 App 已保存的登录文件，不发起自己的 OAuth，不额外要一次授权。 - 按 region 注册模型分组：三家各自的 region 各注册成一个 provider，可以同时开启；没有账号的 region 不注册。 - 账号分发：WorkBuddy 支持优先使用、轮询、临期积分优先和会话固定账号，并在限流或额度用尽时自动换号；Trae、Qoder 支持轮询与临期积分优先。 - 积分自动化：自动签到默认关闭。开启后的定时任务与「立即运行」执行同一轮，包含三家的签到、WorkBuddy 国内账号的连登和任务奖励及猫猫旅行。 - 输入框积分：开启 `showComposerPoints` 后，输入区显示当前模型使用的账号余额，点开可换号。 - 面板：账号状态、池状态、模型勾选、连接检查都在插件页的 WTQ Pool 卡片里。模型目录启动时加载，缓存过期后按需刷新，空闲不轮询。 ## 安装 本地包：在源码目录执行 `pnpm install && pnpm run build && npm pack --pack-destination dist`，再安装生成的 `.tgz`： ```powershell $package = (Resolve-Path .\dist\dsh-wtq-pool-1.0.2.tgz).Path dsh plugin --profile desktop add $package ``` 使用实际 profile 名替换 `desktop`。若 `dsh` 不在 PATH，使用安装目录中的 CLI。也可按 npm 包名 `dsh-wtq-pool` 或仓库地址安装。 **面板在哪儿**：侧边栏进 **插件**，点 **dsh-wtq-pool** 那张卡片（或它旁边的 **配置**），完整面板嵌在卡片里。模型分组没出现时，按面板顶部的提示重启 dsh。 ## 使用 在各家桌面 App 中登录后，点击「重新检测账号」。WorkBuddy 支持读取多个已保存登录，5.6 起的 `$wbEncrypted` 登录通过本机 WorkBuddy 获取密钥。Trae 国内版有 Trae CN 与 TRAE SOLO CN 两个登录位；Qoder 每个安装仅保存一个登录，重新登录会覆盖前一个。 顶层选来源，下面三屏： - **账号池**：每个号的标签、剩余积分、额度到期时间、冷却状态、签到进度；可单独停用某个号，或指定某个 region 优先用哪个号。WorkBuddy 的分发有优先用一个、轮流使用、优先使用临期积分、同一对话固定；Trae 与 Qoder 有轮流使用和优先使用临期积分。 - **模型**：勾选这个 region 要暴露的模型，未勾选的不进模型选择器。可改显示名、上下文窗口、输出上限、思考等级和贴图支持。一个模型组最多发布 64 个，超出的标「未发布」，网关仍会服务它们。 - **连接检查**：逐条报出网关在不在听、模型目录读到几个、注册的地址与实际绑定的是否一致、每个 provider 有没有被宿主接受，并可复制整份报告。 签到可单账号执行，也可在标题栏一次领完该来源。自动签到默认关闭，开启后默认于 09:00（北京时间）执行，错过时段将在下次启动补领。Trae 的每日签到是一台设备一次，Qoder 的新一轮在每天 10:00（北京时间）开出。 ## 设置 | 键 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `enabled` | `true` | 关闭后网关不启动 | | `sourceWorkbuddy` / `sourceTrae` / `sourceQoder` | `true` | 关闭后该来源不扫描、不发布、不请求 | | `distribution` | `priority` | WorkBuddy 池的发放方式：`priority` 先用一个，`round-robin` 均摊，`expiry` 优先消耗临期积分，`sticky` 同一对话固定 | | `sourceDistributions` | `{}` | Trae、Qoder 的分发方式：`round-robin` / `expiry`；兼容旧值 `priority` | | `cooldownSeconds` | `60` | 限流冷却时长。上游报出重置时间时以它为准，按北京时间 | | `authFile` | `""` | WorkBuddy 登录文件路径；扫描其所在目录的全部 `.info` 登录，留空自动发现 | | `autoCheckin` | `{"enabled":false,"hours":[9]}` | 自动签到的开关与时点，`hours` 为北京时间整点，留空用 09:00 | | `creditReserves` | `{}` | 按账号 id 设定的积分保底，余额低于它的账号不参与分发 | | `showComposerPoints` | `false` | 在输入区显示当前账号积分 | 模型勾选和首选账号由面板保存。命令面板里也可打开面板、重新检测、清除冷却、全部签到、连接检查。 ## 端口 ``` WorkBuddy 42831 / 42841 Trae 42851 / 42861 Qoder 42871 / 42881 ``` 以上为首选端口。被占用时网关绑定临时端口，运行时 provider 注册使用本次实际地址，面板显示回退结果。国内模型仅使用国内账号。 ## 数据与出网 只读三家 App 的本机登录文件，不写回登录状态。provider 通过运行时注册接入，不改写宿主 provider 配置；插件设置仍由宿主持久化至 profile。令牌仅在插件进程中使用，并发往对应厂商接口。网关仅监听 `127.0.0.1`；面板资源与 RPC 只接受实际回环对端，不信任代理转发头，因此远程浏览器不能直接使用面板。插件不直接管理或删除宿主会话记录。 同一台机器上的其他进程可以调用这些回环端点，从而消耗已登录账号的额度。 令牌只会发往以下主机： - WorkBuddy：`copilot.tencent.com`、`www.codebuddy.cn`、`www.codebuddy.ai`、`www.workbuddy.ai`、`www.workbuddy.cn` - Trae：`api.trae.cn`、`solo.trae.cn`、`trae-api-cn.mchost.guru`、`coresg-normal.trae.ai`、`growsg-normal.trae.ai` - Qoder：`gateway.qoder.com.cn`、`openapi.qoder.com.cn`、`api3.qoder.sh`、`openapi.qoder.sh` 插件不发送遥测。面板外链仅在用户点击时打开。 ## 开发 ```sh pnpm install pnpm run build # 产出 lib/（宿主半为 ESM，客户端半为 CJS） pnpm run typecheck # 宿主半 pnpm run typecheck:client pnpm test # Node 自带测试，离线回归 ``` `src/host.ts` 是引擎（账号发现、池、网关、面板通道），`src/index.ts` 是 Cordis 入口（设置 schema、provider 注册、面板路由），`src/pi-compat.ts` 把宿主能力适配成引擎已在用的那套调用，`src/client/` 是面板与输入区的 React 半。 ## 致谢 若干模块移植或参考自下列 MIT 项目，特此鸣谢： | 项目 | 版权 | 用于 | | --- | --- | --- | | [XDTrees/dsh-workbuddy-xdpool](https://github.com/XDTrees/dsh-workbuddy-xdpool) | (c) 2026 XDTrees | WorkBuddy 账号池与整体移植来源 | | [corrinehu/dsh-workbuddy-connect](https://github.com/corrinehu/dsh-workbuddy-connect) | (c) 2026 Corrine Hu | 回环端点的安全模型 | | [dingminhua/dsh-connect-workbuddy](https://github.com/dingminhua/dsh-connect-workbuddy) | (c) 2026 LaoDing | 上游接口与错误分类 | | [dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae](https://github.com/dingminhua/dsh-connect-trae) | (c) 2026 dingminhua | Trae 协议参考 | | [eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-qoder](https://github.com/eghrhegpe/dsh-connect-qoder) | (c) 2026 eghrhegpe | Qoder 协议参考 | ## 许可 MIT，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。
